title: Ben Thanh Market
text: Ben Thanh Market is a central market in Ho Chi Minh City. Visitors can browse souvenir shops, local products, clothing stalls, and food counters.

title: Nguyen Hue Walking Street
text: Nguyen Hue is a pedestrian boulevard linking the City Hall area with Bach Dang Wharf. It is a popular place for an evening walk.

title: Saigon Central Post Office
text: Saigon Central Post Office is a historic architectural landmark in the central area of Ho Chi Minh City, close to Notre Dame Cathedral.

title: Notre Dame Cathedral
text: Notre Dame Cathedral is a well-known historic cathedral in central Ho Chi Minh City. It stands near Saigon Central Post Office.

title: Saigon Opera House
text: Saigon Opera House is a historic performing-arts landmark near Dong Khoi Street in the city center.

title: Cho Lon Chinatown
text: Cho Lon is Ho Chi Minh City’s Chinese quarter. Visitors can explore local streets, traditional markets, and temples.

title: Binh Tay Market
text: Binh Tay Market is a large trading market in the Cho Lon area. It is especially associated with wholesale commerce.

title: Thien Hau Pagoda
text: Thien Hau Pagoda is a temple in Cho Lon that honors the sea goddess Thien Hau. It is a destination for visitors interested in religious and cultural heritage.

title: Jade Emperor Pagoda
text: Jade Emperor Pagoda is a religious landmark that visitors can include while exploring Ho Chi Minh City.

title: Cu Chi Tunnels
text: The Cu Chi Tunnels are an underground tunnel network northwest of central Ho Chi Minh City. They are connected to the history of the Vietnam War.

title: Com Tam
text: Com tam is a popular Ho Chi Minh City dish made with broken rice. It is commonly served with savory accompaniments.

title: Banh Xeo
text: Banh xeo is a crispy Vietnamese savory pancake associated with southern-style street food.

title: Banh Mi
text: Banh mi is a Vietnamese filled bread sandwich and is widely enjoyed as a street-food option in Ho Chi Minh City.

title: Tan Son Nhat International Airport
text: Tan Son Nhat International Airport serves Ho Chi Minh City and is about seven kilometers from the city center.

title: Airport Transfer Options
text: For the trip between Tan Son Nhat Airport and the city center, travelers can use a taxi, a ride-hailing service, or a city bus.

title: Weather in Ho Chi Minh City
text: Ho Chi Minh City is generally warm throughout the year. The rainy season usually runs from around May to November.

title: 42 Nguyen Hue Building
text: The building at 42 Nguyen Hue is known for small shops and other businesses occupying an older city building.
